newsitem.title: USA: US exporters cannot confirm Argentine corn switch.
newsitem.headline: US exporters cannot confirm Argentine corn switch.

text.p: Several U.S. exporters said they could not confirm market talk that about 400,000 tonnes of Argentine corn purchased by an unspecified buyer was switched to U.S. origin in the last few days.
"I heard the rumor this morning (Thursday)," one U.S. exporter said. "I don't have any idea if that is true or not. I know we are not doing anything like that. It would not necessarily surprise me."
The switch would depend on destination and position. "If it is nearby, it does not work unless you figure some way to get rid of the freight you have booked against it," he said.

But he noted the Argentine corn basis has been relatively firm. "It could be that the advantage has been switched back to the (U.S.) West Coast if the corn was going to a Far East destination," the exporter said.
For the June position, Argentine corn Upriver/South was at $121.85 a tonne, FOB, while U.S. no. 3 yellow corn was at $125.00, FOB, U.S. Gulf and at $132.85, FOB Pacific Northwest.
"It might make sense to sell your Argentine and buy Pacific Northwest premiums," he said. "But I have not seen the activity on the PNW to confirm that kind of action. Nobody knows."
"The rumor has been floating around. It is not necessarily a fact. Talking to our people, we have not confirmed that has happened," a second U.S. exporter said.

A third U.S. exporter said if the switch occurred it would have been done a few days ago. He said the amount of corn was difficult to quantify and could be anywhere from 100,000 tonnes up to 500,000 tonnes.
"We cannot confirm it. I don't think any one player is doing it. I think there is some spot stuff that is being switched back, a cargo here, a cargo there," he said.
Corn futures on the Chicago Board of Trade ended higher partially bolstered by talk of the switch, traders said.
CBOT corn for May delivery closed 3-1/2 cents higher at $2.98-1/2 a bushel and while July also closed up 3-1/2 cents at $2.96-3/4.
"That may be what is going on. CBOT corn is rallying off of something," an exporter said.
